correctness.rationale: The source vertex orbit premise is established in the inspected 2022 full paper and reproved by greedy rearrangement. Probability of exposing a fixed rank-s vertex follows by independent Gaussian signs and exchangeable positive ranks, with the saturated orbit counted by a binomial upper tail. Layer cake with N_t~Bin(m,q(t)) gives an exact finite width integral and Gaussian radial normalization. Dominated convergence with integrable q(t) gives the scaling limit; differentiating the integral determines the C2/non-C3 boundary and the binomial CLT yields the clipped-normal critical law. Analytical proof covers all stated parameters. Standalone standard-library replay passed 30 complete small angular enumerations, 1,360 support comparisons, two planar width formulas and three large-dimensional checks. No computation is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Normal-cone spherical measures and Euclidean mean width are canonical geometric invariants of a natural, widely studied two-parameter polytope family. The theorem completely describes random exposed-vertex orbit probabilities and quantifies an abrupt capped-positive-rank crossover: a critical clipped-normal angular law and a limiting mean-width profile that is exactly C2 but not C3 at ratio 1/2. This goes beyond routine rewriting of known facet, volume, inball, diameter or Löwner classifications, and can be used to measure typical optimization geometry and stochastic sampling of partial permutohedra.
